parameters.formDescription:
=DeepResearcher is a multi-step, recursive approach using the internet to solve complex research tasks, accomplishing in tens of minutes what a human would take many hours.

To use, provide a short summary of what the research and how "deep" you'd like the workflow to investigate. Note, the higher the numbers the more time and cost will occur for the research.

The workflow is designed to complete independently and when finished, a report will be saved in a designated Notion Database.

values.fieldLabel: What would you like to research?

values.option: =I understand that higher depth and breadth values may mean longer wait times and higher costs. I acknowledge this and wish to proceed with the research request.

parameters.text:
=You are an expert research assistant helping a user refine their research request before deep research begins.

Given the user's query below, analyze what is ambiguous, underspecified, or could significantly change the direction of the research depending on the answer. Then generate up to 3 clarifying questions that are directly relevant to THIS specific topic, not generic questions that could apply to any query.

Guidelines:
- Each question must be something that would meaningfully change what gets researched or how the report is structured, not a surface-level or filler question
- Reference specific terms, entities, or concepts from the user's actual query in your questions, do not ask generic questions like "what time period?" unless time period genuinely matters for this topic
- If the query is already narrow, specific, and unambiguous, return fewer questions, or none at all, do not force 3 questions if they aren't needed
- Avoid questions the user has likely already implicitly answered within their query
- Phrase each question concisely, in plain language, as something a sharp human researcher would actually ask before starting work

<query>{{ $json.prompt }}</query>

Return a maximum of 3 questions. Return fewer if the query is already clear.

messageValues.message:
=You are an expert researcher. Today is {{ $now.toLocaleString() }}. Follow these instructions when responding:
 - You may be asked to research subjects that is after your knowledge cutoff, assume the user is right when presented with news.
 - The user is a highly experienced analyst, no need to simplify it, be as detailed as possible and make sure your response is correct.
 - Be highly organized.
 - Suggest solutions that I didn't think about.
 - Be proactive and anticipate my needs.
 - Treat me as an expert in all subject matter.

 - Value good arguments over authorities, the source is irrelevant.

 - You may use high levels of speculation or prediction, just flag it for me.

parameters.content:
## 2. Ask Clarifying Questions
[Read more about form nodes](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.form/)

To handle the clarification questions generated by the LLM, I used the same technique found in my "AI Interviewer" template ([link](https://n8n.io/workflows/2566-conversational-interviews-with-ai-agents-and-n8n-forms/)).
This involves a looping of dynamically generated forms to collect answers from the user.

## 6. Perform DeepSearch Loop
[Learn more about the Looping in n8n](https://docs.n8n.io/flow-logic/looping/#creating-loops)

The key of the Deep Research flow is its extensive data collection capability. In this implementation, this capability is represented by a recursive web search & scrape loop which starts with the original query and extended by AI-generated subqueries. How many subqueries to generate are determined the depth and breadth parameters specified.

"Learnings" are generated for each subquery and accumulate on each iteration of the loop. When the loop finishes when depth limit is reached, all learnings are collected and it's these learnings are what we use to generate the report.

## 3. Create Empty Report Page in Notion
[Read more about the Notion node](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/app-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.notion/)

Some thought was given where to upload the final report and Notion was selected due to familiarity. This can be easily changed to whatever wiki tools you prefer.

## 4. Trigger DeepResearch Asynchronously
[Learn more about the Execute Trigger node](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.executeworkflow/)

n8n handles asynchronous jobs by spinning them off as separate executions. This basically means the user doesn't have to wait or keep their browser window open for our researcher to do its job.

Once we initiate the Deepresearcher job, we can close out the onboarding journey for a nice user experience.

## 7. Generate Search Queries
[Learn more about the Basic LLM node](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/cluster-nodes/root-nodes/n8n-nodes-langchain.chainllm/)

Much like a human researcher, the DeepResearcher will rely on web search and content as the preferred source of information. To ensure it can cover a wide range of sources, the AI can first generate relevant research queries of which each can be explored separately.

## 8. Web Search and Extracting Web Page Contents using [Tavily](https://tavily.com)
[Read more about the HTTP Request node](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.httprequest/)

Each search query is sent to the Tavily Search API, which returns the top 5 results together with the page content as markdown. A separate scraping step is therefore not needed.

Setup: add your Tavily API key as a Bearer Auth credential on the Web Search node.

## 5. Set Report to In-Progress
[Read more about the Notion node](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/app-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.notion/)

## 9. Compile Learnings with Reasoning Model
[Read more about the Basic LLM node](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/cluster-nodes/root-nodes/n8n-nodes-langchain.chainllm/)

With our gathered sources, it's now just a case of giving it to our LLM to compile a list of "learnings" from them. For our DeepResearcher, we'll use OpenAI's o3-mini which is the latest reasoning model at time of writing. Reasoning perform better than regular chat models due their chain-of-thought or "thinking" process that they perform.

The "Learnings" are then combined with the generated research goal to complete one loop.

## 10. Generate DeepSearch Report using Learnings
[Read more about the Basic LLM node](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/cluster-nodes/root-nodes/n8n-nodes-langchain.chainllm/)

Finally! After all learnings have been gathered - which may have taken up to an hour or more on the higher settings! - they are given to our LLM to generate the final research report in markdown format. Technically, the DeepResearch ends here but for this template, we need to push the output to Notion. If you're not using Notion, feel free to ignore the last few steps.

## 11. Reformat Report as Notion Blocks
[Learn more about the Markdown node](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.markdown/)

To write our report to our Notion page, we'll have to convert it to Notion "blocks" - these are specialised json objects which are required by the Notion API. There are quite a number of ways to do this conversion not involving the use of AI but for kicks, I decided to do so anyway. In this step, we first convert to HTML as it allows us to split the report semantically and makes for easier parsing for the LLM.

## 13. Update Report in Notion
[Read more about the HTTP request node](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.httprequest/)

In this step, we can use the Notion API to add the blocks to our page sequentially. A loop is used due to the unstable Notion API - the loop allows retries for blocks that require it.

## 1. Let's Research!
[Learn more about the form trigger node](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.formtrigger)

n8n forms are a really nice way to get our frontend up and running quickly and compared to chat, offers a superior user interface for user input. I've gone perhaps a little extra with the custom html fields but I do enjoy adding a little customisation now and then.

## 12. Append URL Sources List
[Read more about the Code node](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.code)

For our source URLs, we'll manually compose the Notion blocks for them - this is because there's usually a lot of them! We'll then append to the end of the other blocks.

### 🚏 The Subworkflow Event Pattern 
If you're new to n8n, this advanced technique might need some explaining but in gist, we're using subworkflows to run different parts of our DeepResearcher workflow as separate executions.

* Necessary to implement the recursive loop mechanism needed to enable this workflow.
* Negates the need to split this workflow into multiple templates.
* Great generally for building high performance n8n workflows (a topic for a future post!)

### Recursive Looping
The recursive looping implemented for this workflow is an advanced item-linking technique. It works by specifically controlling which nodes "execute once" vs" execute for each item" because of this becareful of ermoving nodes! Always check the settings of the node you're replacing and ensure the settings match.

=You are are an expert and insightful researcher.
* Given the following prompt from the user, write a final report on the topic using the learnings from research.
* Make it as as detailed as possible, aim for 3 or more pages, include ALL the learnings from research.
* Format the report in markdown. Use headings, lists and tables only and where appropriate.

<prompt>{{ $('JobType Router').first().json.data.query }}</prompt>

Here are all the learnings from previous research:

<learnings>
{{
$('JobType Router').first().json.data
 .all_learnings
 .map(item => `<learning>${item}</learning>`) 
 .join('\n')
}}
